[Music] My name is Princey Varghese, and this is my husband, Jince.
We are from a place called Kolenchery in Ernakulam district. I am a nurse, and I was working in Israel.
It has been 13 years this month since I started working there.
When my daughter was just one year and a 3 months old, I went to Israel. My husband and daughter were at home. I was living alone there.
For the past two to three years, I’ve had this thought in my heart—O Mother Mary, thank You!
I’m so grateful that God gave me the grace to come to this altar and give this testimony. I can’t express how much joy that brings me.
I am standing here today only because of the grace of Mother Mary and Jesus—thousands and thousands of thanks to them!
My second son, Jeron Jince, was born in Israel, in Tel Aviv. He is now two and a half years old.
After he was born, and about three and a half months had passed, we had to bring him back to India
because, according to the law in Israel, we cannot keep a baby there for more than 3.5 months
It wasn’t possible—citizenship there is only given to Jewish people.
That made me feel very distressed in my heart. I cried out to God: “Lord, all these years I couldn’t raise my elder daughter myself…”
And now, when I finally have a son, I can’t even keep him with me.
I was upset thinking, “I have to stay away from both my children again.”
After that, a new desire came into my heart—that somehow, my family and I could go to another country, a better country.
That longing passed through my heart. My friend Anitha is in Australia. She told me:
“Why don’t you write the PTE exam?” But I told her, “I don’t have the confidence. I haven’t written English in so long. Even if I write it, I might not pass.
Why should I go through the pain of failing?” I didn’t have the courage to even try.
But she insisted a lot: “Just write it once. Maybe God will grant it to you.”
For 12 years, I had only been living a routine life—not in any deep faith. I was just working regularly.
I would only pray basic things: “Lord, please protect me. Keep me safe.” That was the only kind of direct conversation I had with God.
I was not someone who used to call on Mother Mary a lot. I am someone who belongs to the Jacobite Church.
We do believe in Mother Mary, but we weren’t used to calling on her so much.
It was during that time, when my heart was so burdened, that I wrote the PTE exam—and somehow, by God’s grace, I got a good score.
I received an Australian qualifying score. I was so happy—I felt like, “Yes, I do have some ability. I can manage English.”
At that point I felt, "I should’ve taken this exam a little earlier." That thought came to me.
With that thought, I decided to move forward. I started looking into Australian immigration through agencies. I was about to turn 39.
Everyone told me, “You should have started this earlier. Why are you trying at this age?”
“It’s going to be difficult now. At least a study visa could have been an option if you had tried before 35.”
That made me feel like my dream had ended.
Continuing to live alone in Israel, away from my children, wasn’t going to be easy anymore.
Even though I had a husband, it was really hard for him to handle the children alone.
He said, “We must try somehow. Let’s do whatever is needed.”
That’s when my good friend Shanty, who had taken a covenant here at Kreupasanam for her daughter to go to Australia—I knew about it—
She hadn’t expected to get it. But miraculously, her daughter Lismi got it.
That really impacted me. I thought, “If they received it, maybe through the intercession of this Mother, she could ask Jesus for mine too…”
“Maybe what didn’t happen before might be possible now.” So I thought, “Let me also try.”
That’s when my friend Jincy said, “Chechi, I’m coming to see you.”
She came to me one day, prayed, anointed my forehead with the Kreupasanam holy oil, and said:
“Chechi, it’s been so long, hasn’t it? You should try to live as a family now. Be with your children.”
“You’ve been separated from them for so long. It’s time to be united.”
I said, “I don’t know whether all this will actually work, Jincy.” But she said:
